claims.statement: Visibility guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES. GHEC managed-user enterprises offer Private/Internal, while non-managed-user enterprises offer Private/Public; other declared products use Public/Private. Internal is not a universal GHEC project option.

Public project audience is everyone on internet; private requires at least read project access; GHEC internal allows enterprise members. These source audience descriptions are not effective target reader tests or approval to broaden access.

Project visibility does not grant underlying repository permission; private-repository items require repository access. This guarantee does not independently prove every draft, custom field, README or aggregate metadata safe for public display.

Organization owners manage visibility and may permit project admins; user owner/admin manages user project visibility. General access guide admin claim must be qualified by effective organization restriction.

Organization owners can restrict changes to organization owners; enterprise-owner restriction appears only under project-visibility-policy feature, which resolves GHEC only. Do not infer same enterprise policy availability across GHES/FPT.

Private and GHEC internal organization projects display avatars of users currently updating project. UI presence exposes collaboration metadata and does not certify identity, audit completeness or authorization.
Danger-zone visibility selection mutates audience; configuration alone does not prove actual permission enforcement or recovery after reverting. No setting changed or project content published.
Linked policy/access pages remain separate evidence; all claims reference-only with no policy adoption, rights clearance, independent published assurance or native rollout.
